messages.content: San Diego got one more wrinkle. Final packet says Friday's last session ends at 3:45 now, not 2:30. Checkout at the conference hotel is still noon and Mark lands around 6. I don't want to redo the split stay. Can you give me the final action list? Also make sure my Tuesday seat is still a window and, for Sunday with Mark, paired seats would be best if one can be by a window.

The split stay still works; Friday just becomes a bag-management day. I would not try to move bags to the waterfront hotel before the afternoon session. Friday morning: check out at the Marriott, leave the suitcase with bell services, and keep only laptop, charger, meds, and anything you need for the last session. After the 3:45 end, retrieve bags and rideshare to the waterfront hotel; target 4:30-5:00 check-in, then text Mark the room number.
Should I ask for a late checkout anyway since the session is in that hotel?

Yes, ask, but treat it as a bonus. If they give you 1:00, you can repack at lunch and still bell-check before the last block. If they say no, checking out before the morning session is cleaner than gambling on the lunch break.
What should I say to the waterfront hotel about the room? Balcony nice, but I don't want to trigger an upcharge.

Use this: We arrive Friday after a conference, and my spouse arrives separately that evening. If available, please place us in a quiet upper-floor king room away from elevators; a balcony would be appreciated, but please do not change the booked room type or add an upgrade charge. Please note late arrival if check-in is delayed.
Perfect. What do I actually need to call each hotel about?

Call the Marriott to confirm post-checkout luggage storage, bell-desk hours, and whether a late checkout can be requested at check-in. Call the waterfront hotel to confirm check-in time, bag hold if you arrive before the room is ready, Mark arriving separately, and that room note. Flight check: review Tuesday seat now and at check-in; keep the window if still assigned. For Sunday, look for adjacent seats with at least one window, and only pay if the free map would split you or leave you stuck in middles.

messages.content: Switching gears to Boise or Meridian. I need a first plan for a three-night analyzer rollout: training Wednesday and Thursday, and maybe a Tuesday equipment receipt. The client has not decided whether it is the Meridian specialty hospital or a smaller Nampa lab. Can you sketch flights, hotel zones, and whether this is a rental car trip before I push them for details?
Yes. Before I rank it, are you thinking Tuesday to Friday, and is the training case traveling with you or being shipped? The Tuesday receipt time matters a lot for how much arrival buffer you need.

Likely fly Tuesday, home Friday, three hotel nights. One checked training case is possible but not confirmed. If Tuesday receipt happens, it will be after 3. For hotels, keep it well reviewed; I use a gym or pool if it is there, and a hot tub is nice, but not worth a silly commute. I'd like to leave after lunch if it doesn't make Tuesday stressful.

Then I would build two versions. Flight version one: if Tuesday receipt is real, take a late-morning or midday Denver-to-Boise nonstop that lands around 1. That leaves time for baggage, a car pickup, and a drive to Meridian or Nampa before 3. Flight version two: if Tuesday is only a travel day, the afternoon nonstop is fine. I would not add a connection just to preserve a later departure; with a checked case, the nonstop is cleaner.
Can you split Meridian versus Nampa? That's the part making me wobble.

If the site is Meridian, the best zone is Eagle Road, Overland Road, or The Village area: short hospital commute, plenty of food, and easy airport access. Rental car is helpful with a case but not absolutely required if the hotel and hospital are close. If the site is Nampa, stay near I-84 or Idaho Center and keep a car; rideshares are thinner and you do not want to depend on them with equipment.
The Meridian hospital may be near Eagle and Overland. The Nampa lab is west side, but they have not sent an address.

With those probable locations, I would rank the zones: 1) Meridian/Eagle Road as the best hedge, 2) Nampa/I-84 if the lab is confirmed, 3) Boise airport or downtown only if you need a neutral fallback. Meridian to west-side Nampa can still be 25-35 minutes, but downtown can be just as much drive without helping your workdays.
So downtown Boise is too cute by half?

A little, unless the hotel quality gap is huge or you have an evening commitment downtown. It is nicer for dinner, but it adds parking and morning traffic. For this trip, a well-reviewed suburban hotel near the actual site beats a prettier lobby farther away.
What about car versus rideshare? I hate renting a car that sits there, but I also hate juggling the case.

Decision rule: if the case travels with you, book a compact SUV. It protects the equipment, makes loading easier, and gives you control if the client changes rooms or timing. If the case is shipped and the site is Meridian, rideshare can work, especially with a hotel very close to the hospital. If the site is Nampa, I would keep the car either way.
Give me a boss-ready recommendation, but conditional.

Recommend holding a Tuesday late-morning or midday nonstop to Boise, a Friday morning or midday return, a cancellable Meridian/Eagle Road hotel, and a cancellable compact SUV until the site and case are confirmed. If Meridian wins and no case travels, cancel the SUV and use rideshares. If Nampa wins or the case travels, keep the SUV and switch the hotel to the best-reviewed Nampa/I-84 option if it is strong enough.
And what questions do I send the client so we can stop maintaining two plans?

Ask for the final training address, room location, and Wednesday/Thursday start times; whether Tuesday equipment receipt is required and the exact time; whether they can receive and secure the training case before you arrive; parking, loading dock, and badge instructions; and whether they have a preferred nearby hotel. Once those are answered, the plan should collapse quickly: buffered nonstop plus car if Tuesday or the case is firm, later nonstop plus rideshares only if it is Meridian and light.

messages.content: Client finally answered: Meridian specialty hospital near Eagle and Overland, Tuesday equipment receipt is 3:30, and I have one checked case. Flights are basically 11:05 nonstop landing 12:55, or 2:20 nonstop landing 4:10. Afternoon is nicer, but I assume that second one is a trap? Hotel choice is also annoying: Meridian place is 4.4, seven minutes away, indoor pool and fitness, free parking, no hot tub listed. Downtown is 4.5 with pool, hot tub, and gym, but 22 to 30 minutes away.

Take the 11:05 nonstop. The 2:20 landing at 4:10 misses the 3:30 receipt on paper, and in real life you would still need baggage claim, rental pickup, and the drive. For the hotel, choose the Meridian property. Losing the hot tub is annoying, but the shorter commute and simpler case handling are worth more on this rollout.
So don't try to land, grab the case, and show up late with an apology?

No. That makes the first operational handoff fragile. The 11:05 gives you a normal path: land 12:55, get the checked case around 1:20-1:30, pick up the car, grab a quick lunch if needed, and still arrive at the hospital around 2:30-2:45. Even a moderate delay leaves you a little room.
The Meridian hotel has breakfast too. I just keep looking at the downtown hot tub after standing all day.

For this trip, stay close. You gain 45 minutes to an hour across the workdays, avoid downtown parking, and make it easier to move the case. Call the Meridian hotel once to verify the hot tub status because amenities are sometimes incomplete online, but do not move downtown just for that feature.
Hotel nights are Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, right? Home Friday?

Yes: Tuesday through Thursday nights in Meridian, fly home Friday. Since Thursday wraps around 4:30 and you have shipping paperwork and repacking, a Thursday-night departure would be tight and prone to mistakes with the case.
Agreed. For Friday, do I take the earliest nonstop or leave myself a little morning space?

Leave yourself a little morning space if the fare is reasonable. A late-morning or midday nonstop is better than a dawn scramble after repacking. If the only nonstop is very early, I would compare it against a one-stop with a short, clean connection, but do not accept a long layover just to avoid the early alarm.
For the car, compact SUV again or is a sedan fine?

Compact SUV. One checked case plus work bag is easier to load, and the slightly higher cargo space helps at the hospital parking area. Pick up at BOI shortly after arrival Tuesday and return before the Friday flight. Skip prepaid fuel unless the rate is unusually good; you will not drive enough to make it worthwhile.
Let's make that the booking plan. Main cabin, and if the seat map is decent grab windows.

Booking plan: Tuesday 11:05 DEN-to-BOI nonstop, main cabin, checked training case, and a window seat if available. Hotel: the well-reviewed Meridian/Eagle-Overland property Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday nights; request a quiet room away from elevators, and ask whether a hot tub exists but keep the location priority. Car: compact SUV from BOI Tuesday early afternoon to Friday return. Friday flight: choose a late-morning or midday nonstop if available. Confirm before finalizing: hospital loading door, parking, who signs for the 3:30 equipment receipt, secure case storage overnight, hotel parking, and any late-arrival note.
